subjects.label: Launch promises versus what shipped
subjects.description: The gap between what was promised or shown before release and what the launch build actually held, including calling it a scam or still waiting for the promised features to arrive; ordinary patch notes and the later recovery belong elsewhere.

subjects.label: The comeback
subjects.description: The game's reputation reversing through years of free updates: it gets better every year, players flipping their review to positive, the redemption arc, the awards for ongoing support; a single patch or bug fix is not this.

subjects.label: Exploring planets and the universe
subjects.description: Flying between systems and landing on planets to see what is there, the scale of the universe, getting lost on a world, and whether the planets feel distinct or are variations on a theme; space combat and building are separate rows.

subjects.label: Ships, frigates and freighters
subjects.description: Starships, frigates and capital-class freighters as possessions: wanting bigger ones, upgrading them, building or styling your own; base building and on-foot play do not belong here.

subjects.label: Base building
subjects.description: Placing, upgrading and dismantling bases and their parts, and the resource gathering that feeds them; ships and general crafting talk do not belong here.

subjects.label: Direction and goals
subjects.description: Whether the sandbox gives you objectives or leaves you aimless: no real goals beyond a thin main story, lacking direction, feeling lost with no idea what to do next; how many hours it lasts and whether individual systems are explained are separate rows.

subjects.label: Held up against the big studios
subjects.description: Measuring this game against AAA studios and their games and finding the big names wanting: Starfield by comparison, not even Kojima, the big publishers should learn from this; a plain statement of what genre it is does not belong here.
